extracted.intended_audience: Cochrane review authors, Cochrane peer reviewers, and editors of intervention systematic reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and mandatory criteria for conducting, reporting, and peer-reviewing Cochrane intervention systematic reviews (MECIR). Intended to guide authors in preparing reviews and reviewers/editors in judging methodological and reporting quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item classification: Mandatory vs Highly Desirable
rubrics_metrics.description: Each MECIR item is classified as Mandatory (must be met or justified) or Highly Desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory items must be met or justified; failure to meet Mandatory items is grounds for not publishing. Highly Desirable items are recommended but not absolute requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: C1 PICO clearly specified
rubrics_metrics.description: PICO clearly specified (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the scope of the review using explicit PICO components so reviewers and readers can assess relevance and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: C2 Pre-specify outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-specify outcomes including primary and secondary outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly identify primary vs secondary outcomes in protocol to avoid selective outcome reporting; justify choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: C3 Pre-specify subgroup analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-specify subgroup analyses; classify as a priori vs post hoc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document which subgroup analyses were planned a priori and which are exploratory/post hoc; interpret post hoc findings cautiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: C4 Search key databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Search at least CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure search comprehensiveness by including major bibliographic sources appropriate to intervention reviews; document search dates and sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: C5 Justify search restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify any restrictions by language, publication year, or status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any limits (e.g., language, date, publication type) need explicit justification to avoid biased evidence selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: C6 Search trial registers and conference proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Search trials registers and conference proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include grey literature and trial registries to reduce publication bias and capture unpublished or ongoing studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: C7 Search reference lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Search reference lists of included studies and relevant reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handsearching reference lists and related reviews helps identify studies missed by database searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: C8 Document search strategies in full
rubrics_metrics.description: Document search strategies in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete, reproducible search strings for each database and date run so searches can be replicated and assessed for adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: C9 Re-run searches close to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-run searches close to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update searches prior to finalizing the review to include recently published studies; document the updated search date.

rubrics_metrics.name: C10 Independent duplicate screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Two reviewers independently screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent dual screening of titles/abstracts and full texts to reduce selection bias and errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: C11 Resolve screening disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolve disagreements with a third reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a predefined process (third reviewer or consensus) for resolving conflicts to ensure consistency and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: C12 Document reasons for exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Document reasons for exclusion at full-text stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit reasons for exclusion (ideally in an exclusions table) to support transparency and the PRISMA flow diagram.

rubrics_metrics.name: C13 Piloted data-extraction form
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a piloted data-extraction form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot extraction forms on a sample of studies to ensure clarity, completeness, and consistency in captured data.

rubrics_metrics.name: C14 Independent duplicate data extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Two reviewers independently extract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent duplicate extraction reduces data-entry errors and bias; discrepancies should be resolved by consensus or third reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: C15 Contact study authors for missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact study authors when data are missing or unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempt to obtain missing or unclear information from study authors and report responses (or lack thereof).

rubrics_metrics.name: C16 Use appropriate risk-of-bias tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool for randomised trials, ROBINS-I for non-randomised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the recommended RoB instruments appropriate to study design to evaluate internal validity systematically.

rubrics_metrics.name: C17 Independent duplicate risk-of-bias assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Two reviewers independently assess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent assessments reduce subjectivity; disagreements should be resolved and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: C18 Justify each RoB judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify each judgement with a quote / citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide supporting evidence (quotes, page numbers, citations) for each risk-of-bias judgement to allow verification and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: C19 Pre-specify meta-analytic methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-specify meta-analytic methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define methods (effect measures, pooling methods, model choices) a priori in protocol to avoid analytical flexibility and selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: C20 Justify fixed vs random effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify choice of fixed vs random effects model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the rationale for model selection based on heterogeneity, clinical diversity, and inferential goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: C21 Investigate heterogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate heterogeneity (I², Tau²).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify and explore heterogeneity using statistics (I², Tau²) and consider subgroup or meta-regression analyses where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: C22 Plan and conduct sensitivity analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan and conduct sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify sensitivity analyses to test robustness of findings (e.g., excluding high RoB studies, alternative effect measures) and report results.

rubrics_metrics.name: C23 Investigate publication bias threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate publication bias when ≥10 studies (funnel plot, Egger's test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use funnel plots and statistical tests (e.g., Egger's) to explore small-study effects when there are enough studies (generally ≥10).

rubrics_metrics.name: C24 Use GRADE per outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Use GRADE to rate certainty of evidence per outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply GRADE systematically for each important outcome and present results in summary-of-findings tables; justify downgrades/upgrades.

rubrics_metrics.name: R1 Plain Language Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain Language Summary written for non-specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an accessible summary that communicates key findings, certainty, and implications in language understandable to patients and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: R2 Structured abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract follows Cochrane structured format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Cochrane abstract structure to present background, methods, results (with effect estimates and certainty), and conclusions succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: R3 Background content
rubrics_metrics.description: Background includes description of condition, intervention, why review needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualise the review by explaining the health condition, intervention rationale, and gaps the review addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: R4 Replicable methods section
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods section is sufficient to allow replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed methods (searches, selection, extraction, analyses) so others can reproduce the review's conduct and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: R5 PRISMA flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: PRISMA flow diagram of study selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a flow diagram showing numbers of records identified, screened, excluded (with reasons), and included to document study selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: R6 Characteristics tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristics of included and excluded studies tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tables summarising study characteristics for included studies and reasons for key exclusions to aid appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: R7 Forest plots
rubrics_metrics.description: Forest plots for each outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present effect estimates and confidence intervals graphically (forest plots) for each outcome and comparison to aid interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: R8 Summary-of-findings tables with GRADE
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary-of-findings table per comparison using GRADE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present per-comparison and per-outcome findings with effect sizes, absolute risks where appropriate, and GRADE certainty ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: R9 Discussion content
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion addresses summary, completeness, certainty, biases, agreements with other reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss main findings, evidence completeness, certainty/limitations, potential biases, and how results align with existing literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: R10 Distinguish implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions distinguish implications for practice and for research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate actionable implications for clinical practice from recommendations for future research, reflecting evidence certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Norm 1: Question relevance and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Question relevance and clarity — PICO well-formed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must assess whether the review question is relevant to stakeholders and whether the PICO is clearly and appropriately specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Norm 2: Search comprehensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Search comprehensiveness — were appropriate databases searched without unjustified restrictions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether search strategy and sources were adequate and whether any restrictions (language, date, publication type) were justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Norm 3: Bias reduction in selection/extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias reduction in study selection and data extraction — independent duplicate screening?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for processes reducing bias (dual independent screening/extraction, resolution of disagreements) and spot-check these processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Norm 4: Validity of synthesis methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity of synthesis methods — was meta-analysis appropriate? Heterogeneity adequately investigated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether pooling was appropriate given heterogeneity and prespecified methods, and whether heterogeneity analyses were conducted and interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Norm 5: Risk-of-bias assessment quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk-of-bias assessment quality — was RoB 2 applied correctly with substantiated judgements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure RoB tools appropriate to study designs were used, judgements are supported by evidence, and any disagreements are documented and plausible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Norm 6: GRADE certainty ratings justification
rubrics_metrics.description: GRADE certainty ratings — are downgrades/upgrades justified per outcome?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that GRADE judgments per outcome are transparent, justified, and consistent with reported risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, and publication bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Norm 7: Honesty of conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Honesty of conclusions — do conclusions match the certainty of evidence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag overstated conclusions that exceed the GRADE certainty and ensure conclusions accurately reflect the strength and limits of the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Norm 8: Conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicts of interest — declared by review authors and assessed by reviewer?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that authors declared potential conflicts and consider whether COIs could bias review processes or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Norm 9: Reporting completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting completeness — does the review meet PRISMA + Cochrane structural requirements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess completeness of reporting (PRISMA items, Cochrane-specific outputs like SoF tables) to ensure transparency and usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive Norm: Conclusions limited by GRADE
rubrics_metrics.description: No conclusion may be stronger than its GRADE certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must flag any conclusions that overstate findings relative to the outcome-level GRADE certainty; ensure wording of conclusions matches certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive Norm: Disagreement as quality signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Disagreement among study quality assessors is itself a quality signal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a review reports 100% agreement on quality assessments, reviewers should question this; documented disagreements can indicate thorough, critical assessment rather than a flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive Norm: Spot-check extractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer must check at least one included-study extraction against source paper as a spot check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform at least one verification of extracted data against the original study to detect extraction errors or misinterpretations.
